09:00.headline: Myth: coaches will find him
09:00.topic: Myth-buster: coaches can't evaluate players they don't know about; families should learn where the numbers fit and reach out
09:00.caption:
Will college coaches find your player on their own?

It's one of the most common recruiting myths. ❌

A coach can only evaluate a player he knows about. Waiting to be discovered can mean he's never seen by the programs that fit him best.

✅ Know where his numbers fit: exit velo, 60 time, velocity, pop time, grades
✅ Build a list of programs at the levels where he fits
✅ Reach out with his numbers, video and schedule

Being proactive isn't pushy. It's how coaches learn who he is.

Has your family started reaching out to coaches yet? 👇

See what the numbers say about your player's best fit:

13:00.headline: 4 numbers coaches check
13:00.topic: Know your level: the measurables (exit velo, 60, throwing velo/pop time, GPA) that come up in recruiting conversations
13:00.caption:
Do you know which numbers coaches look at first?

Every program evaluates a little differently, but a few measurables come up in almost every recruiting conversation:

⚾ Exit velocity: how hard he hits the ball
⚾ 60-yard dash: his speed
⚾ Throwing velo or pop time: arm strength for his position
⚾ GPA and transcript: whether he can be admitted and stay eligible

Numbers aren't the whole picture. Coaches also weigh video, game performance, makeup and fit. But knowing where his numbers stand helps you focus on the levels where he has real options: D1, D2, D3, NAIA or JUCO.

Which of these do you know for your player today? 👇
